task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about Loom Lantern Press's move into audiobooks and the production, rights and sales work behind making a small backlist audible.

facts.text: A July 2026 production note records narrator Iri Venn stopping a recording to check a place-name pronunciation with Loom Lantern Press's editor.
The independent publisher has 14 print backlist titles and selected three for a proposed audio pilot.
Audio permission has been agreed with the authors of two selected works; negotiations for the third remain unfinished.
The publisher's print agreements do not all include the same audio rights, according to the supplied contract summary.
The first completed audiobook is the original fictional novel Tide Keys, read by Venn and edited by a contracted sound engineer.
Its completed production cost was $6,000, including narration, editing and quality checks, but not the publisher's general overhead.
Under the supplied terms for individual retail downloads, the publisher retains $10 per sale after the retailer's deduction and the author's allocation.
Recovering that $6,000 production cost at an unchanged $10 contribution would require 600 paid downloads, before other costs.
The retail report for the title's first six sales weeks, July 20 through August 30, 2026, lists 120 paid downloads and $1,200 in publisher receipts under those terms.
The first six weeks do not establish lifetime sales or the profitability of the entire audio program.
Publisher Mara Quill says some print readers want audio for commuting while other listeners may never buy a physical copy.
Quill said, "A book we already printed still needs a new set of work before somebody can listen to it."
Venn marks breaths, names and character changes in a working script rather than recording every page successfully in one pass.
Venn said, "A quiet recording is not just a quiet room. It is all the decisions you stop and check."
The publisher has not measured how many audio buyers would otherwise have bought the print edition.
Library and subscription-platform deals are being discussed separately and do not necessarily pay the same $10 contribution as an individual retail download.
The second authorized title has not yet completed recording, so its final duration and production cost are unknown.
A planned launch event was moved from a bookshop to a community listening room because the bookshop could not accommodate headphones for the expected group.
Loom Lantern began with local travel essays in 2016 and now publishes fiction and memoir.
No outside investor, guaranteed audio-sales contract or decision to stop printing books has been announced.

forbidden_additions: All three titles are authorized and completed or 120 sales have recovered $6,000
The individual-download contribution applies to every distribution channel or audio replaces print by decision
